# Review — iliad-103 (16.394–476)

Two passes. Pass 1 read units.json and new-renderings.md against packet.md, conventions.md and the house table (grepped), ../odyssey/conventions.md, the published units (searched by script on the letters of `t`, and again line by line with breathings and accents stripped) and the archive (cross-references). Pass 2 re-read every unit as edited, read gloss.json (it was present) and checked every parse and every known-form entry against its line, and checked new-renderings.md against the units word by word. `t` was not touched (checked: the list of `t` strings is identical before and after every edit script). Edits to units.json and gloss.json were made by script. No modern translation was consulted.

Counts. Pass 1: 1 high, 28 medium, 21 low (50). Pass 2: 6 medium, 11 low (17 rows: units 1 medium + 1 low; gloss.json 5 medium + 9 low; new-renderings.md 1 low row covering three word-for-word mismatches), plus the follow-on rewrites listed at the end, which carry pass 1 changes into new-renderings.md.

## Checked and found right

- Greek equals a published unit and l/i identical: 401 (iliad-081), 426 (iliad-025), 439 (iliad-006, 021), 440 (iliad-006, 021, 050, 089), 444 (iliad-021, 029 and seven Odyssey units), 458 (iliad-021), 469 (odyssey-096). 400, 418, 424–425, 462, 469, 473 are inside differently cut units and reuse the published wording as far as the sentence allows (400 identical; 418 identical; 424–425 identical but for the closing mark; 462 identical; 473 only "my" → "his", recorded).
- Quotation marks: 3 opening and 3 closing in each layer; Sarpedon “ on 422, ” on 425; Zeus “ on 433, ” on 438; Hera “ on 440, ” on 457; `mark` on the first unit of each (422, 433, 440). Last unit of iliad-102 (392–393) is narrative, no speech runs in. No speech runs out at 476.
- Paragraph flags p at 394, 419, 426, 439, 458, 462, as in the packet. ln of every unit is its first line; the units concatenate to the packet text exactly (checked by script).
- Scansion flags: none; no line hand-scanned.
- All forms are covered (425 forms: 88 novel in gloss.json, the rest in the glossary); every entry has the shape "lemma — meaning", typographic ’ only, novel entries under 230 characters; every broaden entry begins with the old entry whole.

## Considered and refused

- 395 "Aeolic form with -μεν": the label is traditional and defensible (the glossary says "epic -έμεν"); left.
- 394 l "had cut off" for an aorist after ἐπεί: the same pattern is shipped ("when they had gathered", iliad-001).
- 396 "(the Scamander)", "(Troy’s wall)": identifications a reader needs; the river and wall are the poem’s own; left.
- 401/466 δεύτερον ὁρμηθείς "next" in i against "second" in l: i is free English; the phrase has the same l word.
- 419 note names Erymas of 16.345 and the Rhodian Tlepolemus: these are checkable cross-references (16.345 verified in the archive), not claims about the Greek of these names; left.
- 419 l "girdle" against the note’s "belt-guard": the sense is declared uncertain; recorded in new-renderings.
- 428 l "crook-taloned" / i "hook-taloned": exactly the Odyssey table’s split (22.302).
- 431 l "pitied them" repeating τοὺς: τοὺς is object of both participle and verb; harmless in l.
- 435–438 i "have him subdued": a decided reading, recorded as such in new-renderings (Zeus would hand him over).
- 449 "heroes who are children of gods": the interpretation follows from Sarpedon being named; left.
- 459 "old gloss ‘drops’" for ψιάδας: the note says the sense is from context and the origin unknown; no translation is cited.
- 463/455 i "Then" for ἔνθ’ ἤτοι: i is free; l now has "There indeed" in both places.
- 466 l omits μέν after αὐτοῦ: a particle left untranslated in l is house practice here.
- Gloss ἔπι: no explicit "on, after its noun" reading, but the entry’s head sense "on, upon" and the five "placed after its noun" readings cover πέτρῃ ἔπι; left.
- ἀλείς, ἀΐσθων, ῥυτῆρσι are not in new-renderings as formulas: they are single rare words, handled by the notes; the epithets that will recur are listed.

## Open

- The build and validator were not run (reviewer works on the draft only). Points the gate will check that I have verified by script: `t` concatenation, quotation balance, no backtick in a note, note lengths 25–110 words, same-Greek-same-English against published Iliad units. The validator’s Odyssey warning for 457 is resolved (the English is now the Odyssey’s).
- 16.443 now differs from the packet’s silence: it is a repeated line the packet did not list because ἔρδ’ and ἕρδ’ differ in breathing. The lead may want `packet.py` to compare with breathings stripped.
